title: Mapping-space criterion for a horn-cocartesian edge
statement:
Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and spaces as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], composition of mapping spaces (precomposition by an edge) as in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and inner fibrations and horn-cocartesian edges as in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $p:E\to B$ be an inner fibration between quasicategories in a fixed universe, and let $s:x\to y$ be an edge of $E$. The edge $s$ is $p$-cocartesian in the horn-lifting sense if and only if, for every vertex $z$ of $E$, precomposition with $s$ and with $p(s)$ gives a homotopy pullback square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}
\operatorname{Map}_E(y,z)&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_E(x,z)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
\operatorname{Map}_B(p(y),p(z))&\longrightarrow&\operatorname{Map}_B(p(x),p(z)).
\end{array}$$
A homotopy pullback square of spaces means that the canonical map from its upper left corner to the path-space homotopy fiber product of the other three corners is a weak homotopy equivalence. No existence of other cocartesian lifts is assumed.

source.place: Proposition 2.4.4.3, printed p. 131, opposite-category dual; Proposition 2.4.1.8 and Remark 2.4.1.4 identify the cartesian-edge definition with its horn criterion. Read online 2026-10-17. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical assertion; WANTED: archived source.

proof.text:
We use join coslices to give a strict representative of the coherent square, as in the dual of HTT's proof. For a diagram $a:K\to C$, put $(C_{a/})_m=\{h:K\star\Delta^m\to C\mid h|_K=a\}$, with restriction operators on $\Delta^m$, and let its projection to $C$ restrict to that last factor. The join is the degreewise join specified by [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones]. For vertices $v,z$, write $L_C(v,z)=(C_{v/})\times_C\{z\}$; explicitly these are maps $\Delta^{m+1}\to C$ with first vertex $v$ and entire remaining face constant at $z$. We will use the following consequence of the cited pushout-join assertion. For any monomorphism $i:K\hookrightarrow K'$ and inner fibration $p:C\to D$, restriction gives a left fibration
$$C_{a/}\longrightarrow C_{(a|_K)/}\times_{D_{(pa|_K)/}}D_{pa/},\qquad a:K'\to C.$$
Indeed, lifting a left horn $\Lambda_j^m$, $0\leq j<m$, amounts exactly to extending across
$$(K'\star\Lambda_j^m)\cup_{K\star\Lambda_j^m}(K\star\Delta^m)\hookrightarrow K'\star\Delta^m.$$
This is inner anodyne by the opposite of the cited pushout-join assertion. To see precisely what this dualization does, define $X^{\mathrm{op}}_r=X_r$ with operator for $\alpha:[u]\to[r]$ given by the operator for $\alpha^{\mathrm{rev}}(a)=r-\alpha(u-a)$ on $X$. Reversal takes $\Lambda_j^m$ to $\Lambda_{m-j}^m$, interchanges the two join factors, and preserves inner horns. It therefore converts a left-horn inclusion in the second factor into the right-anodyne inclusion in the first factor required by that assertion. An inner fibration lifts an inner-anodyne map: extend along the generating horns, use the previously chosen compatible extensions at each successor stage and their union at a limit stage, and pass to a retract. Taking $K=\varnothing$ and $D=\Delta^0$ also proves that every $C_{a/}\to C$ is a left fibration when $C$ is a quasicategory. These constructions only use $p$ being inner; they impose no existence of cocartesian lifts.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.1 and Lemma 2.1.2.3, applied to coslices; dual pushout-join argument written out.

proof.text:
Apply Step 1 with $K=\{0\}\subset K'=\Delta^1$ and $a=s$. This gives a left fibration
$$\phi:E_{s/}\longrightarrow Q:=E_{x/}\times_{B_{p(x)/}}B_{p(s)/}.$$
By [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], $\phi$ is a trivial Kan fibration exactly when it lifts every $\partial\Delta^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, including $m=0$. Such a lifting problem is, by the displayed coslice definition, exactly a lifting problem over $B$ for
$$(\Delta^1\star\partial\Delta^m)\cup_{\{0\}\star\partial\Delta^m}(\{0\}\star\Delta^m)\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\star\Delta^m.$$
Number the vertices $0,1,2,\ldots,m+2$, with the first two carrying $s$. The domain contains the face omitting $1$ and every face omitting a vertex $2,\ldots,m+2$, and omits exactly the face omitting $0$. It is therefore $\Lambda_0^{m+2}\hookrightarrow\Delta^{m+2}$ with prescribed edge $\{0,1\}=s$. Conversely every horn in the definition of $p$-cocartesian is obtained this way by $m=n-2$. Consequently the horn-cocartesian condition on $s$ is equivalent to $\phi$ being a trivial Kan fibration. In particular the dimension-zero boundary test is the $\Lambda_0^2$ test, so no lifting condition has been lost.

source.place: Definition 2.4.1.1 and Remark 2.4.1.4, opposite dual; boundary/horn correspondence in the proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3.

proof.text:
For each vertex $z$ of $E$, restrict the last-factor projection to define
$$T_E(s,z)=E_{s/}\times_E\{z\},\qquad T_B(p(s),p(z))=B_{p(s)/}\times_B\{p(z)\}.$$
The fiber of $\phi$ over the vertex $z$ of this projection is the map
$$\phi_z:T_E(s,z)\longrightarrow L_E(x,z)\times_{L_B(p(x),p(z))}T_B(p(s),p(z)).$$
All four spaces here are Kan. Indeed, the coslice projections are left fibrations by Step 1, hence their vertex fibers are left fibrations over a point; apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] after the reversal defined in Step 1. The same relative-coslice construction, with $K=\varnothing$ and $K'=\{x\}$, says that $L_E(x,z)\to L_B(p(x),p(z))$ is a left fibration. Its target is Kan, so the same reversed right-fibration result makes it a Kan fibration. Thus the displayed pullback is Kan, and $\phi_z$ is a left fibration over that Kan complex, hence a Kan fibration too. Pullbacks preserve lifting properties directly: pull a horn problem back to the original map and use its filler. This justifies every restriction just made.

Now $\phi$ is trivial if and only if every $\phi_z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. In the forward direction its restrictions are trivial Kan fibrations, and [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion] makes them weak equivalences. Conversely, if every $\phi_z$ is a weak equivalence, that same criterion says all its vertex fibers are contractible Kan complexes. Every vertex of $Q$ projects to some $z\in E_0$, and its fiber for $\phi$ equals its fiber for $\phi_z$. Hence all vertex fibers of the left fibration $\phi$ are contractible. The reversed form of [lem-coef-right-fibration-contractible-fibers] makes $\phi$ a trivial Kan fibration. Reversal preserves Kan conditions, boundary lifting, and weak contractibility: on realizations it is the homeomorphism reversing barycentric coordinates. This also covers empty vertex fibers without assuming a lift exists in advance.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3, fiberwise test; Lemma 2.1.3.3 and Lemma 2.1.3.4, with left/right reversal.

proof.text:
For each $z$ consider the strictly commutative square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}T_E(s,z)&\longrightarrow&L_E(x,z)\\
\downarrow&&\downarrow\\
T_B(p(s),p(z))&\longrightarrow&L_B(p(x),p(z)).\end{array}$$
The horizontal maps restrict to the initial vertex of $s$ or $p(s)$; the vertical maps apply $p$. Its ordinary pullback comparison is exactly $\phi_z$. Its right vertical map is a Kan fibration by Step 3. Therefore [lem-coef-kan-pullback-path-comparison] identifies that ordinary pullback with the path-space homotopy pullback by a weak homotopy equivalence. Two-out-of-three for the induced maps on components and homotopy groups shows that this strict square is a homotopy pullback if and only if $\phi_z$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3, final paragraph; Lemma 2.4.4.1 in its dual form.

proof.text:
Restriction to the final vertex $1$ of $s$ gives $r_1:E_{s/}\to E_{y/}$. It is a trivial Kan fibration. A boundary lifting problem for it becomes the inclusion
$$(\Delta^1\star\partial\Delta^m)\cup_{\{1\}\star\partial\Delta^m}(\{1\}\star\Delta^m)\hookrightarrow\Delta^1\star\Delta^m.$$
Here $\{1\}\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is the generating right horn $\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$. The first assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-anodyne-cocones], with the other inclusion the boundary inclusion, makes this join inclusion inner anodyne. Since $E$ is a quasicategory it has the required filler (the extension argument of Step 1). For $B$, replace the prescribed map $s$ by $p(s)$ in this very inclusion; its inner-anodyne property is unchanged, and the quasicategory horn fillers of $B$ supply the extensions. Restricting over $z$ or $p(z)$ and using [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] consequently gives natural equivalences
$$T_E(s,z)\xrightarrow{r_1}L_E(y,z),\qquad T_B(p(s),p(z))\xrightarrow{r_1}L_B(p(y),p(z)).$$
The statement applies also to $m=0$: the join inclusion is the inner horn $\Lambda_1^2$, not an unproved existence of a cocartesian lift.

source.place: Proposition 2.1.2.5 (right-anodyne coslice variant), derived here from Lemma 2.1.2.3; used in the dual proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-left-pinch-comparison] to $C=E$ and $C=B$. It supplies the natural left-pinch maps $j^L:L_C(a,b)\to U_C(a,b)$ and identifies them as homotopy equivalences. Together with the right-pinch model already fixed in [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], this gives the strict arrow-space models used for the two horizontal maps.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3, paragraph specifying the strict representative; Kerodon Proposition 4.6.5.10 (01L5), opposite/left-pinch form.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-fixed-edge-prism-coherence] to $p:E\to B$, the edge $s$, and each vertex $z$. Its fixed-edge triangle prisms give the roof $U_C(y,z)\leftarrow T_C(s,z)\to U_C(x,z)$ and prove that the roofs for $E$ and $B$ commute strictly under $p$. Hence, after inverting the left legs, the resulting coherent square is exactly the precomposition square in the item, including its commutation homotopy.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 2.4.4.3, paragraph specifying the strict representative; Kerodon Construction 4.6.8.9 (01PF), fixed-edge prism and naturality.

proof.text:
We compute the homotopy-pullback test using the strict roof presentation specified in Step 7. First replace the two right corners of Step 4 by $U_E(x,z)$ and $U_B(p(x),p(z))$, composing the horizontal maps with $j^L$. There is a strict map from the old square to this square: identity on its two left corners and $j^L$ on its two right corners. The three-corner cospans therefore satisfy exactly the strict commutation equations of [lem-coef-kan-homotopy-pullback-invariance], and all three corner maps are homotopy equivalences. The induced map of path homotopy pullbacks is a weak equivalence; the fourth-corner comparison maps commute with it, so two-out-of-three proves that the two strict squares have the same homotopy-pullback test.

The new square is the simultaneous roof representative of the canonical coherent precomposition square: its two left corners are $T_E(s,z)$ and $T_B(p(s),p(z))$, related naturally by $j^Lr_1$ to the intended arrow mapping spaces at $y$ and $p(y)$. To compute a homotopy limit for a square given by these roofs, retain this strict representative before inverting those equivalences. To use right-pinched spaces, retain also the natural roofs $L_C(a,z)\xrightarrow{j^L}U_C(a,z)\xleftarrow{j^R}\operatorname{Map}_C(a,z)$ at every corner. Every comparison in this presentation commutes with $p$ on simplices, so the same strict-cospan invariance applies to each change of model. The resulting comparison is therefore the one for the stipulated coherent square. No arbitrary commutation homotopy, and no purported simplicial operation concatenating interval paths, is needed. Combining Steps 2, 3 and 4 now gives
$$s\text{ is horn-}p\text{-cocartesian}\iff\phi\text{ is trivial}\iff(\forall z,\ \phi_z\text{ is a weak equivalence})\iff(\forall z,\ \text{the stated mapping square is a homotopy pullback}).$$
Neither direction used existence of cocartesian lifts of any other edge.
